questions.stem_latex:
A buoy is suspended in the ocean. At its lowest point, the buoy is at a height of 16 metres above the sea floor. At its maximum height, it reaches 28 metres above the sea floor.

The tide mimics a sinusoidal wave, such that one full cycle of the tide going both in and out occurs in 30 hours.

parts.label: a
parts.latex:
If the buoy is initially at its highest point, show that the buoy follows an equation above sea level of

$$h(t)=6\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi t}{15}\right)+22$$

where $h(t)$ is the height of the buoy above the sea floor in metres after $t$ hours.

parts.label: b
parts.latex: State the number of times the buoy reaches a level of 20 metres above the sea floor in the first 60 hours.

parts.label: c
parts.latex: If the buoy was at its highest point above the sea floor at 2 a.m on Monday, at what times does the buoy reach 20 metres above the sea floor within the next 60 hours. Leave your answer to the nearest minute.

solutions.latex:
\exfigure{995_q15_s1}

Step 1

$f(x)=e^{-x}(1+x)$

$u=e^{-x}$, $v=1+x$

$\dfrac{du}{dx}=-e^{-x}$, $\dfrac{dv}{dx}=1$

$$\begin{aligned}f'(x)&=u\dfrac{dv}{dx}+v\dfrac{du}{dx}\\&=e^{-x}+(1+x)(-e^{-x})\\&=e^{-x}(1-(1+x))\\&=-xe^{-x}\end{aligned}$$

Step 2: for stationary points, $f'(x)=0$

$-xe^{-x}=0$

$x=0$, or $e^{-x}=0$ (no solutions)

When $x=0$: $y=\dfrac{1+0}{e^0}=1$

$(0,1)$

Step 3: determine nature of stationary point

$f'(x)=-xe^{-x}$

$u=-x$, $v=e^{-x}$, $\dfrac{du}{dx}=-1$, $\dfrac{dv}{dx}=-e^{-x}$

$$\begin{aligned}f''(x)&=u\dfrac{dv}{dx}+v\dfrac{du}{dx}\\&=-x(-e^{-x})+e^{-x}(-1)\\&=e^{-x}(x-1)\end{aligned}$$

At $x=0$: $f''(x)=e^0(-1)=-1<0$

$\therefore(0,1)$ is a local max

Step 4: determine POI

$f''(x)=0$

$e^{-x}(x-1)=0$

$e^{-x}=0$ (no solutions), $x=1$

When $x=1$: $y=e^{-1}(1+1)=\dfrac{2}{e}$

$$\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}x&0&1&2\\\hline\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}&-1&0&\dfrac{1}{e^2}\end{array}$$

When $x=2$: $f''(x)=e^{-2}(2-1)=\dfrac{1}{e^2}>0$

Since change in concavity, $\left(1,\dfrac{2}{e}\right)$ is a POI
solutions.marks_breakdown: 1: Attempts differentiation using product or quotient rule; 1: Correct stationary point; 1: Determines nature of stationary point through $f''(x)$ and sub $x$ value; 1: Determines POI (not awarded if concavity change not tested); 1: Graph with key points

Cover year 2024 printed; sat 21 February 2024 (Year 12, Term 1), so year 2024. The school name appears only as a crest image on the cover (The King's School). Question-paper cover table lists Q8 3 marks and Q15 7 marks (matches the questions: Q8 1+2, Q15 2+5); the scanned mark-scheme cover table lists Q8 /5 and Q15 /5 (same total of 10, so Section II still 45). Mark scheme labels Q13(c) as '(d)'. Typos in the mark scheme transcribed as written, for the owner to check: Q2 acute angle written as pi/3 (sin^-1(1/2) is pi/6; the count of 4 solutions is unaffected) and x=0 written with a degree sign; Q3 working written 'n = pi f' with n = 6 (the coefficient of x), then T = 1/f = pi/6; Q14(c) theta list gives 3.1937 where 8.1937 is meant (t=39h 7min is right); Q12(b) tables headed dy/dx in the scan but values are d2y/dx2. Q14(c) scheme times: 11:07 am Mon, 10:53 pm Mon, 5:07 pm Tue, 4:53 am Wed. Q4 has no printed option text (A-D are points on the diagram). Q9(a), Q12(a)(ii) and Q15(b) are sketches on blank space: no axes are printed so no question figure. No misnumbering. Paper uses unitalicised 'sin', 'cos', 'ln', 'log' in the equation editor; written with LaTeX operators. Q9 data row and Q10/Q11 statistics content is Standard-course (MST-11-08) not Advanced; flagged via standard_topic. Q1 Pareto chart not tagged (not named in the Standard syllabus text).
